source: It is not the case that the policy is fair and effective. The policy is fair. Therefore the policy is not effective.

reconstruction.title: Argument about Policy Fairness and Effectiveness

claims.text: It is not the case that the policy is fair and effective.

evidence.quote: It is not the case that the policy is fair and effective.

claims.text: Therefore the policy is not effective.

evidence.quote: Therefore the policy is not effective.

formalization.domain_description: Non-empty domain of policies (though propositional logic doesn't require individual domain details)

translations.reason: Translates 'not (fair and effective)' as logical negation of conjunction

interpretation_notes: Using propositional logic with two atomic propositions F and E
The argument structure is purely classical propositional: ¬(F∧E), F ⊢ ¬E
No need for first-order elements like predicates or quantifiers
